title: Two recessive parents
hook: Combine the alleles and inspect the four possibilities.

knows: Each parent in this model contributes one allele.
doesNotKnow: How the aa by aa cross distributes combinations.

misconception: An allele from one parent determines the whole offspring genotype.
objective: Use a Punnett square to count have two recessive alleles (aa) in the aa by aa cross.

claims.text: Question, grid and reveal: In a simple one-gene model, parents aa and aa each pass on one allele. Each gamete shown is equally likely. How many of the four possible combinations have two recessive alleles (aa)? The four combinations are aa, aa, aa, aa. 4 of the four have two recessive alleles (aa). This model assumes equally likely gametes and a single gene; it does not predict the outcome of a particular birth.
Each square represents an equally likely combination under the stated model; siblings are not guaranteed to match the proportions.
Recall: each parent contributes one allele to each combination.

recall.question: In this one-gene model, how many alleles does each parent contribute to an offspring?
recall.why: Each parent contributes one allele through a gamete in the stated model.
